extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, hearing officers, and attorneys involved in USPTO disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural requirements and standards for imposing an interim suspension of a practitioner from practice before the USPTO under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25, and the immediate steps and notifications that follow (notice, opportunity to respond, limited recognition, referral, filing deadlines, publication, account dissociation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for interim suspension under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25
rubrics_metrics.description: Interim suspension may be ordered when there is evidence that a respondent committed a serious crime (here, a felony conviction for Menacing, Domestic Violence). The OED Director may file a Request for Notice, Order, Interim Suspension, and Referral pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.25.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order was mailed by certified mail and provided Respondent an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing the imposition of an interim suspension. In this matter the Respondent stipulated to the interim suspension, and the stipulation meant there was 'no genuine issue of material fact' under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25, making interim suspension appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary basis: violation of 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.804(b) and 11.804(i)
rubrics_metrics.description: The interim suspension was ordered for violation of 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.804(b) and 11.804(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order ties the disciplinary action to the respondent's guilty plea and sentencing in a state criminal proceeding (felony Menacing, Domestic Violence; misdemeanor Child Abuse) and references those criminal convictions as the factual basis for the violation of the cited disciplinary provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral to hearing officer under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b)(5)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Complaint is to be referred to a hearing officer for the purpose of conducting a formal disciplinary proceeding, pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referral initiates a formal disciplinary process separate from the interim suspension, with the hearing officer handling the proceeding in accordance with the cited regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to file written answer under 37 C.F.R. § 11.36 within 30 days
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must file a written answer to the Complaint within thirty (30) days from the date of the Final Order with the hearing officer in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.36.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The answer must be filed at the specified mailing or hand-delivery addresses for the HUD Office of Hearings and Appeals Docket Clerk, and a PDF version must be emailed to the hearing office (alj.alj.@hud.gov). A copy of the answer must also be served on the OED Director by mail to the provided address for Robin Crabb, Associate Solicitor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition to practice for 30 days to facilitate compliance with § 11.58(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is granted limited recognition to practice before the Office commencing on the date of the Order and expiring thirty (30) days after the date the Order is signed, for the sole purpose of facilitating Respondent's compliance with the provisions of 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The limited recognition is narrowly tailored and temporary, expressly to allow the suspended practitioner to take actions required by § 11.58(c) (e.g., client notification/transition obligations reflected by that regulation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Notice of Interim Suspension in the Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice of Interim Suspension in the Official Gazette describing the practitioner's interim suspension and the criminal conviction(s) that prompted it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice text must identify the respondent (name, city, registration number), state the interim suspension under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b) and the underlying conviction (including statutory citation and case number), and provide reference to the OED FOIA Reading Room where disciplinary decisions are available (https://foiadocuments.uspto.gov/oed/).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to USPTO employees, interested agencies/courts, and state bar authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice of the Final Order to (i) appropriate employees of the USPTO; (ii) interested departments, agencies, and courts of the United States; and (iii) appropriate authorities of any state in which the Respondent is known to be a member of the bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a required dissemination step following imposition of interim suspension to inform relevant internal and external authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 (duties of suspended practitioner)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the Final Order does not recite § 11.58's text, the regulation governs the duties of suspended or disbarred practitioners (e.g., notice to clients, file transfer, and protection of client interests), and the Order expressly requires compliance with those duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from USPTO Customer Numbers and electronic accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall dissociate Respondent's name from any Customer Number(s); any USPTO verified Electronic System account(s) associated with those Customer Numbers; any 'MYUSPTO.GOV' account(s); and any other USPTO verified Electronic System account(s) associated with the Respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent is also specifically prohibited from (a) applying for, (b) obtaining, or (c) having his name added to any such Customer Number or USPTO electronic account unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of seeking review does not stay suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If Respondent seeks a review of this suspension, any review shall not operate to postpone or otherwise hold in abeyance the suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for review do not stay the interim suspension; the suspension remains in effect during review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and Order procedural mailing and response timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order initiating the interim suspension process was mailed by certified mail (receipt numbers provided) and provided Respondent with forty (40) days to file a response opposing the interim suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This documents the procedural requirement to provide notice by mail (certified) and a 40-day response window for the initial Notice and Order under the Office's process for interim suspensions.
